about: Curated English landmark card text for cards the audit (scripts/audit-landmark-cards.ts) flags as a bare definition or as leftover Dutch. Each text rests only on sourceQuote, exact sentences from the cited Wikipedia article (| separates quotes); replaces is the card text before. Applied into landmarks.json funFact and facts.json opening by audit-landmark-cards.ts --stage.

overrides.name: Huis Bartolotti
overrides.text: Built around 1617 for Willem van den Heuvel, who inherited a fortune from a childless uncle on condition that he call himself Bartolotti. Its design is attributed to Hendrick de Keyser, and the house bends twice to follow the curve of the Herengracht.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het is circa 1617 gebouwd voor Willem van den Heuvel tot Beichlingen, een van de rijkste Amsterdammers in die tijd, die veel geld had geërfd van een kinderloze aangetrouwde oom, Giovanni Battista Bartolotti, koopman uit Bologna. | In het testament van deze oom stond als voorwaarde vermeld dat hij zich "Bartolotti" moest noemen. | in de trant van Hendrick de Keyser aan wie het ontwerp wordt toegeschreven | Het Huis Bartolotti heeft twee knikken om deze bocht te volgen
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: Het Huis Bartolotti (also Het Bonte Huis) is a canal house at Herengracht 170-172 in Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Co-kathedrale Basiliek van Sint Nicolaas
overrides.text: Adrianus Bleijs designed this Neo-Baroque and Neo-Renaissance church, completed in 1887. In 2021 it received a relic said to be a rib of Saint Nicholas, Amsterdam's patron saint, kept at Egmond Abbey since 1087.
overrides.sourceQuote: The architect Adrianus Bleijs (1842-1912) designed the church based on a combination of several revival styles: the most prominent being the Neo-Baroque and neo-Renaissance. Construction was completed in 1887. | In December 2021, the basilica received a relic of St. Nicholas from Egmond Abbey. Said to be a fragment of the saint's rib, the bone had been in the custody of the abbey since 1087. | Saint Nicholas is the patron saint of both the church and the city of Amsterdam.
overrides.replaces: The Co-cathedral Basilica of Saint Nicholas (Dutch: Co-kathedrale Basiliek van de Heilige Nicolaas) is located in the Old Centre district of Amsterdam, Netherlands, very close to Amsterdam's main railway station.

overrides.name: Eye Filmmuseum
overrides.text: Queen Beatrix opened this building on Amsterdam's north bank in 2012. Its architects, Delugan Meissl, also designed the Porsche Museum, and its archive holds 210,000 cans of acetate film.
overrides.sourceQuote: The Filmmuseum was renamed the Eye Film Institute Netherlands and was officially opened on 4 April 2012, by Queen Beatrix. | plans were announced for a new home on the north bank of Amsterdam's waterfront | The Eye Filmmuseum building is designed by Delugan Meissl Associated Architects, whose other projects include the Porsche Museum in Stuttgart. | The collection includes 210,000 cans of acetate film
overrides.replaces: Eye Filmmuseum is a film archive, museum, and cinema in Amsterdam that preserves and presents both Dutch and foreign films screened in the Netherlands.

overrides.name: Moco Museum
overrides.text: Opened in 2016 in Villa Alsberg, a 1904 townhouse by Eduard Cuypers, nephew of the Rijksmuseum's architect Pierre Cuypers. Its shows have included Banksy and Andy Warhol.
overrides.sourceQuote: Moco Museum in Amsterdam opened in 2016 on Museumplein, in the historic Villa Alsberg, a townhouse designed in 1904 by Eduard Cuypers the nephew of Pierre Cuypers, designer of Amsterdam Central Station and the Rijksmuseum. | included works by artists such as Banksy and Andy Warhol
overrides.replaces: The Moco Museum (Modern Contemporary Museum) is an independent art museum with locations in Amsterdam, Barcelona, and London, dedicated to exhibiting modern and contemporary art.

overrides.name: Heineken Experience
overrides.text: Built in 1867 as the first Heineken brewery, it was the company's main brewery until 1988. It opened to visitors in 1991 and became one of Amsterdam's most popular attractions.
overrides.sourceQuote: The industrial facility was built as the first Heineken brewery in 1867, serving as the company's primary brewing facility until 1988 when a more modern, larger facility was constructed on the outskirts of the city. | In 1991, the brewery opened its doors to the public through a visitor centre | It grew to become one of Amsterdam's most popular tourist attractions
overrides.replaces: The Heineken Experience, located in Amsterdam, is a historic brewery and corporate visitor centre for the internationally distributed Dutch pilsner, Heineken beer.

overrides.name: Mint Tower
overrides.text: Part of the medieval Regulierspoort gate, the tower was rebuilt after a 1618 fire with a spire by Hendrick de Keyser. Its name comes from the guard house beside it, where coins were minted in the crisis year 1672.
overrides.sourceQuote: The tower was originally part of the Regulierspoort, one of the main gates in Amsterdam's medieval city wall. | After the gate went up in flames in a 1618 fire, only the guard house and part of the western tower remained standing. The tower was then rebuilt in Amsterdam Renaissance style in 1620, with an eight-sided top half and elegant open spire designed by Hendrick de Keyser | The name of the tower refers to the fact that the guard house on the side of it was used to mint coins in the 17th century. | so the guard house of the Munttoren was temporarily used to mint coin
overrides.replaces: The Munttoren (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈmʏnˌtoːrə(n)]; "Mint Tower") or Munt ([mʏnt]) is a tower in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

overrides.name: Embassy of the Free Mind
overrides.text: Dan Brown opened the museum in 2017 in the House with the Heads, a 1622 canal house with six heads of Roman gods on its facade. Its library holds over 25,000 books on Hermeticism and alchemy.
overrides.sourceQuote: The Embassy of the Free Mind was opened in October 2017 by author Dan Brown. | The canal house was built in 1622 by Hendrick de Keyser | Six heads adorn the façade. They depict the Roman gods Apollo, Ceres, Mercury, Minerva, Bacchus and Diana. | The museum has a collection of more than 25,000 books on Hermeticism, Rosicrucianism, alchemy
overrides.replaces: The Embassy of the Free Mind is a museum, library and platform for free thinking inspired by the philosophy of the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica collection.

overrides.name: Madame Tussauds Amsterdam
overrides.text: Founded in 1970, it was the first Madame Tussauds in mainland Europe. Since 1991 it has filled the upper floors of a Peek & Cloppenburg clothing store on Dam Square that opened in 1917.
overrides.sourceQuote: Founded in 1970, it was the first Madame Tussauds that was opened in mainland Europe | Madame Tussauds Amsterdam moved into the upper floors of the building of the international chain of clothing stores Peek & Cloppenburg at the Dam Square. | On April 11, 1917, it opened its doors as the second Peek & Cloppenburg store in the Netherlands.
overrides.replaces: Madame Tussauds Amsterdam is a wax museum situated in Amsterdam, the capital city of the Netherlands. It is located in the centre of the city on Dam Square, near the Royal Palace of Amsterdam.

overrides.name: De Balie
overrides.text: In the late 1970s this 19th-century courthouse was to be demolished for an eight-storey hotel. A public campaign saved it, and in 1982 it became the arts centre De Balie.
overrides.sourceQuote: When the 19th-century building of the Amsterdam Cantonal Court was threatened to be demolished in order to build an eight-storey Bouweshotel in the late 1970s | The city council was persuaded, and a good destination for the building was found in art center De Balie in 1982.
overrides.replaces: De Balie is a Dutch organization that produces independent journalistic programs about art, culture and politics. De Balie is located at Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen 10, near Leidseplein in Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Amsterdam University College
overrides.text: Founded in 2008 by the University of Amsterdam and the Vrije Universiteit, the honours college took in its first class in 2009. Its students live and study together on the Science Park campus.
overrides.sourceQuote: AUC was officially founded in 2008, and took up operation with its founding class in 2009. | is a joint initiative of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam | Students live and study together on an international campus located in Amsterdam Science Park.
overrides.replaces: Amsterdam University College is a Liberal Arts and Sciences Bachelor's programme that is a joint initiative of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. AUC is a Honours programme at the Bachelor's level.

overrides.name: Felix Meritis
overrides.text: Built for an Enlightenment society founded in 1776, the building opened in 1788. Beethoven's Ninth had its Dutch premiere in its oval concert hall, of which the Concertgebouw's small hall is a replica.
overrides.sourceQuote: for the new society called Felix Meritis established in 1776 | The building itself was meant to exemplify the Enlightenment ideals the society stood for. | On 31 October 1788 the building of the same name opened its doors. | Thus, Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony and Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique had their Dutch premiere in the concert hall of Felix Meritis. The small hall of the Concertgebouw is a replica of this concert hall.
overrides.replaces: Felix Meritis ('Happy through Merit') is the name of an intellectual society in Amsterdam, but subsequently used for their building on the Keizersgracht.

overrides.name: OT301
overrides.text: Artists squatted this former Dutch film academy in 1999 and bought it from the city in 2006. It is now a cultural centre with a club, cinema and gallery.
overrides.sourceQuote: In 1999, a group of artists squatted the former Dutch film academy. | the building was bought by the user association Eerste Hulp Bij Kunst (EHBK) from the council in 2006 | It has four public spaces (club, cinema, gallery, and kitchen)
overrides.replaces: OT301 is a self-managed social centre in a legalized squat in the Dutch city of Amsterdam, located on Overtoom 301.

overrides.name: Westergasfabriek
overrides.text: When it opened in 1885 it was the largest gasworks in the Netherlands, making coal gas for street lighting until 1967. Most buildings are by Isaac Gosschalk.
overrides.sourceQuote: Westergasfabriek  was ready in 1885 | In 1885 it was the largest gas extraction plant in the Netherlands. The gas was extracted from coal and was used for street lighting. | This is why in 1967 the production of gas from the factory stopped permanently. | Most of the thirteen buildings on site were designed by architect Isaac Gosschalk
overrides.replaces: The Westergasfabriek is a former gasworks in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, now used as a cultural venue.

overrides.name: Pathé Tuschinski Cinema
overrides.text: Abraham Tuschinski opened this Art Deco and Amsterdam School cinema in 1921. Under the occupation he was deported to Auschwitz and murdered by the Nazis in 1942.
overrides.sourceQuote: The theatre was founded by Abraham Icek Tuschinski | the theatre was built in Art Deco, Jugendstil and the Amsterdams School style | On October 28, 1921, the theatre opened its doors | Tuschinski and Gerschtanowitz were deported to Auschwitz and Ehrlich to Sobibor; all three were murdered by the Nazis in 1942.
overrides.replaces: The Koninklijk Theater Tuschinski (English: Royal Theatre Tuschinski) also called Pathé Tuchinski, is a movie theatre in Amsterdam, Netherlands, near Rembrandtplein and belonging to the historic French group Pathé.

overrides.name: Hollandsche Schouwburg
overrides.text: The Nazi occupiers made this theatre a Jewish theatre in 1941 and then used it as a deportation centre. A wall now carries some 6,700 surnames of the more than 100,000 Jews deported from the Netherlands.
overrides.sourceQuote: it was deemed a Jewish theatre in 1941 by Nazi occupiers, and it was later used as a deportation center during the Holocaust in the Netherlands. | a wall engraved with some 6,700 surnames of the more than 100,000 Jewish deportees from the Netherlands
overrides.replaces: The Hollandsche Schouwburg (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɦɔlɑntsə ˈsxʌubʏr(ə)x]; English: Hollandic Theatre) is a museum in Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

overrides.name: ASC SDW
overrides.text: Founded on 10 May 1907, the club's initials stand for Sterk Door Wilskracht, Strong Through Willpower. From 1967 to 1976 it played at the highest Dutch amateur level.
overrides.sourceQuote: ASC SDW (Amsterdamse Sportclub Sterk Door Wilskracht) | De club werd opgericht op 10 mei 1907. | Van het seizoen 1967/68 tot en met het seizoen 1975/76 kwam het negen seizoenen uit op het hoogste amateurniveau
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: ASC SDW (Amsterdam Sports Club Strong Through Willpower) is an amateur football club from Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands.

overrides.name: Begijnhofkapel
overrides.text: After the Beguines lost their church to the Protestants, they built this hidden chapel by joining two of their houses. The city approved it, in 1671, only if it did not look like a church from outside.
overrides.sourceQuote: The Beguines, too, had to hand over the church in their courtyard. | after joining two of the hofje houses bought for that purpose | his nephew laid the foundation stone on 2 July 1671. The Protestant council members of the city of Amsterdam approved the building plans on condition that the building did not look like a church from the outside.
overrides.replaces: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas Parish of Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Westerkerk
overrides.text: Designed by Hendrick de Keyser and inaugurated in 1631, it was one of the first churches purpose-built for Protestants. It is still the largest such church in the Netherlands.
overrides.sourceQuote: The Westerkerk was built between 1620 and 1631 in Renaissance style according to designs by architect Hendrick de Keyser. | inaugurated on June 8, 1631 | The Westerkerk was one of the first purpose-built Protestant churches. It remains the largest church in the Netherlands that was built for Protestants
overrides.replaces: The Westerkerk (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈʋɛstərˌkɛr(ə)k]; English: Western Church) is a Reformed church within Dutch Protestant Calvinism in central Amsterdam, Netherlands.

overrides.name: Jewish Museum
overrides.text: Opened in 1932 in the Waag on Nieuwmarkt, the museum was forced to close under the Nazi occupation and lost much of its collection. Since 1987 it has occupied four former synagogues.
overrides.sourceQuote: The Joods Museum opened its doors on 24 February 1932 and was initially housed at the Waag (Weighing House) on Nieuwmarkt square. Following the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands in World War II, the museum was forced to close and much of the collection was lost. | In 1987, it moved to a new location, occupying four former synagogues
overrides.replaces: The Joods Museum (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌjoːts ɦɪsˈtoːris myˈzeːjʏm]; English: Jewish Museum), part of the Jewish Cultural Quarter, is a museum in Amsterdam dedicated to Jewish history, culture and religion, in the Netherlands and worldwide.

overrides.name: Rembrandt House
overrides.text: Rembrandt bought this house in 1639 for thirteen thousand guilders and lived and worked here until it was auctioned in 1658. Its rooms were refurnished from the inventory of his bankruptcy.
overrides.sourceQuote: Rembrandt bought it on 5 January 1639 for thirteen thousand guilders. After his bankruptcy it was auctioned in 1658 | Between 1639 and 1658, the house was occupied by the Dutch painter Rembrandt van Rijn, who also had his studio and art dealership there. | The building was redesigned in the 20th century on the basis of the inventory that was drawn up during Rembrandt's bankruptcy in 1656.
overrides.replaces: The Rembrandt House Museum (Dutch: Museum Het Rembrandthuis) is a museum located in a former house in the Jodenbreestraat, in the center of Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Plein Theater
overrides.text: Amsterdammers started it in 1982 as a neighbourhood theatre and café in the empty canteen of the former Amstel brewery. Renamed Oostblok in 2015, it took back its old name in 2019.
overrides.sourceQuote: Een groep Amsterdammers startte in 1982 een buurttheater op met een eetcafé, dit in een leegstaande bedrijfskantine van de voormalige Amstelbrouwerij. | In 2015 werd Pleintheater omgedoopt tot Oostblok, maar kreeg in maart 2019 weer de originele naam terug.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The PleinTheater in Amsterdam-Oost is a stage for small-scale theatre, dance, contemporary classical music, youth theatre and neighbourhood activities.

overrides.name: Amsterdam Memorial to the Canadian Liberators
overrides.text: In May 1945 a thousand Canadians entered Amsterdam along the Apollolaan, cheered by about half a million people. Jan de Baat's steel pennant here was unveiled in 1980, when Canadians rode the same route again.
overrides.sourceQuote: 8 mei 1945 | Via de Berlagebrug, de Apollolaan, de Van Baerlestraat, het Leidseplein en het Singel trokken in 1945 duizend Canadezen Amsterdam binnen en gingen naar de Dam. Ongeveer een half miljoen Amsterdammers juichten hen toe. | Op 5 mei 1980 trokken Canadezen over dezelfde route als in 1945 opnieuw Amsterdam binnen. | Het monument is gemaakt door Jan de Baat (1921-2010) en omvat een stalen wimpel die uit de grond rijst in een grasveld.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: Amsterdam dankt zijn Canadezen is a monument in the Canadezenplantsoen, called the Apollolaan before 2020, in Amsterdam, opposite the Apollohal between the Stadionweg and the Bernard Zweerskade.

overrides.name: Cat Cabinet
overrides.text: Bob Meijer founded the museum in 1990 in memory of his red tomcat, John Pierpont Morgan. Its 1667 house on the Golden Bend was a filming location for Ocean's Twelve.
overrides.sourceQuote: in 1990 the museum was founded by Bob Meijer in memory of his red tomcat John Pierpont Morgan | were built in 1667 | in the grand Gouden Bocht ("Golden Bend") of this canal | The museum served as filming location for Ocean's Twelve in 2004.
overrides.replaces: The KattenKabinet ("Cat Cabinet") is an art museum in Amsterdam devoted to works depicting cats.

overrides.name: Martin Luther King
overrides.text: Tired of waiting for permission, artist Airco Caravan installed this bronze of King herself on his birthday, 15 January 2020. The city approved it a few months later.
overrides.sourceQuote: De kunstenaar was het wachten beu en plaatste op eigen initiatief op 15 januari 2020 (de geboortedag van King) een groter, bronzen beeld van King. | De plaatsing van het beeld is enkele maanden later alsnog goedgekeurd door de gemeente
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Image of Martin Luther King is an artistic work of art in Amsterdam-Zuid.

overrides.name: Molen van Sloten
overrides.text: The mill was built in 1991 around an 1847 mill body brought from the Watergraafsmeer. It helps drain the western garden cities and is open to visitors almost every day.
overrides.sourceQuote: Deze molen is gebouwd in 1991 met gebruikmaking van een uit 1847 daterende molenromp afkomstig uit de Watergraafsmeer | zorgt samen met het Akergemaal voor de bemaling van de Westelijke Tuinsteden | De Molen van Sloten is een van de weinige in Holland die (bijna) iedere dag voor publiek geopend is.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Molen van Sloten is a polder mill in the village of Sloten near Amsterdam. It is an oak-wooden, thatched octagonal tower mill on a stone base.

overrides.name: Amstel Academie
overrides.text: Founded in 1961 as the nursing school of the VU hospital, it took the name Amstel Academie in 2004. It trains staff for nearly all the region's care institutions.
overrides.sourceQuote: De Amstel Academie is in 1961 opgericht als zogenaamde verpleegstersschool | dat het toenmalig Ziekenhuis der Vrije Universiteit haar eigen verpleegkundigen zou opleiden | In 2004 kreeg het instituut zijn uiteindelijke naam: Amstel Academie. | De Amstel Academie leidt op voor bijna alle zorginstellingen in de regio
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Amstel Academie is a Dutch academy that specializes in training in the medical sector. The Amstel Academie is located on the campus of the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Torenfort aan de Ossenmarkt
overrides.text: Completed in 1861 for the New Dutch Water Line, this round brick tower fort has walls about 1.8 metres thick. Fully manned, it housed 232 men.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het fort aan de oostkant van de vestingstad Weesp werd in 1861 voltooid en maakte met Weesp deel uit van de Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie. | De muren zijn ongeveer 1,8 meter dik. | Bij volledige bezetting bood het fort onderdak aan 232 man
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Torenfort aan de Ossenmarkt is a tower fort in Weesp in the province of North Holland.

overrides.name: Sloterkerk
overrides.text: Rembrandt drew and etched the earlier church on this site, and his granddaughter Titia van Rijn married in it in 1686. The present church dates from 1861.
overrides.sourceQuote: Rembrandt heeft deze derde kerk in etsen en tekeningen vastgelegd | De kleindochter van Rembrandt, Titia van Rijn, is op 27 juni 1686 in deze kerk getrouwd | In 1861 werd de zaalkerk, een Waterstaatskerk naar ontwerp van P.J. Hamer, in gebruik genomen.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Sloterkerk is a Protestant church in Sloten, North Holland.

overrides.name: Ketelhuis
overrides.text: Started in 1999 as a temporary cinema at the Westergasfabriek, Het Ketelhuis nearly went bankrupt several times before it could stay. It reopened with three screens in 2006.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het Ketelhuis is een Nederlands filmtheater dat sinds 1999 gevestigd is in cultuurpark Westergasfabriek in Amsterdam. | er voor drie jaar een tijdelijke bioscoop in te richten | Na enkele roerige jaren waarin Het Ketelhuis meerdere keren bijna failliet ging, kreeg het na drie jaar toestemming om zich definitief te vestigen in cultuurpark Westergasfabriek. | Op 13 september 2006 ging het vernieuwde Ketelhuis met drie zalen open.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: Het Ketelhuis is a Dutch film theater that has been located in the Westergasfabriek cultural park in Amsterdam since 1999. Dutch films, European arthouse films, documentaries and family films are screened.

overrides.name: Oudemanhuispoort
overrides.text: Built around 1601 as an almshouse for old men and women, it now houses the University of Amsterdam's humanities faculty. Eighteen stalls selling gold, silver and books opened in its passage in 1757.
overrides.sourceQuote: Omstreeks 1601 verrees dit complex als Oudemannen- en vrouwengasthuis | de faculteit der geesteswetenschappen is er gevestigd | In 1757 werden 18 nieuw gebouwde 'kassen' in de doorgang geopend, te koop waren 'goud, zilver, boeken, galanteryen en Neurenburgsche waaren'.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: Oudemanhuispoort (often abbreviated as: OMHP) is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam, between the Spui and the Waterlooplein. It is one of the main locations of the University of Amsterdam, the faculty of humanities is located there.

overrides.name: Obrechtkerk
overrides.text: Joseph Cuypers and Jan Stuyt designed this Romanesque Revival basilica, built between 1908 and 1911. On its tower clock the Roman numerals 9 and 11 are swapped.
overrides.sourceQuote: This Romanesque Revival cruciform basilica was built between 1908 and 1911. It was designed by Joseph Cuypers and Jan Stuyt. | On the tower clock the Roman numerals 9 and 11 are reversed.
overrides.replaces: The Obrechtkerk (Dutch: Kerk van Onze Lieve Vrouw van de Allerheiligste Rozenkrans) (Church of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary) is the common name for the Roman Catholic church located on the Jacob Obrechtstraat, nearby the Vondelpark in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

overrides.name: P.W. Janssen
overrides.text: Bart van Hove's bronze bust of Peter Wilhelm Janssen, entrepreneur, philanthropist and co-founder of the Deli Company, was unveiled in 1908. It stands four metres tall on a Norwegian granite plinth.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het beeld gemaakt door Bart van Hove werd 29 mei 1908 onthuld | Peter Wilhelm Janssen, ondernemer, filantroop en medeoprichter van de Deli Maatschappij | Het gedenkteken bestaat uit een taps toelopende sokkel van Noors graniet, met daarop het bronzen borstbeeld van Janssen. Het heeft een totale hoogte van vier meter.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Monument Peter Wilhelm Janssen is a monument on Bellamyplein in Amsterdam-West.

overrides.name: Anton de Kom
overrides.text: Jikke van Loon's bronze of the resistance hero and writer Anton de Kom was unveiled in 2006, chosen by local residents and a jury. Its plinth quotes his poem: I go to fight; only after victory will I return.
overrides.sourceQuote: vrijheidsstrijder en verzetsman Anton de Kom | In 2005 kozen de bewoners en een jury voor het ontwerp van Van Loon | Het bronzen beeld werd op 24 april 2006 onthuld. | Strijden ga ik! Eerst na d’overwinning kom ik terug. | De laatste regel is afkomstig uit het gedicht Vaarwel, Akoeba vaarwel! van De Kom.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Monument voor Anton de Kom is an artwork in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

overrides.name: Bellevue
overrides.text: The last game of the 1935 World Chess Championship was played here; by accepting a draw, Max Euwe became world champion. The building dates from about 1840.
overrides.sourceQuote: Op 15 december 1935 vond de laatste partij van het Wereldkampioenschap schaken 1935 plaats in Theater Bellevue. | Euwe accepteerde het aanbod en kroonde zich daarmee tot de nieuwe wereldkampioen schaken. | Het oorspronkelijke gebouw aan de Leidsekade dateert uit circa 1840
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: Theater Bellevue is a theater with three rooms on Leidsekade in Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Meervaart Theater
overrides.text: Open since 1977 and named after its street, Meer en Vaart, the centre is where the Cinekid children's film festival began in 1986.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het centrum bestaat sinds 1977 en is vernoemd naar de straat Meer en Vaart, waaraan het is gelegen. | In 1986 begon hier het kinderfilmfestival Cinekid.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: Meervaart is a theater and a convention center in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. Meervaart is a contemporary metropolitan theater where audiences and creators with diverse backgrounds, taste preferences and ambitions come into contact with each other.

overrides.name: Elthetokerk
overrides.text: Cornelis Kruyswijk's Amsterdam School church opened here in 1929 in the presence of Queen Wilhelmina. It was closed and demolished in 1992.
overrides.sourceQuote: De kerk is gebouwd in 1929 naar ontwerp van Cornelis Kruyswijk. De kerk is dat jaar in het bijzijn van koningin Wilhelmina in gebruik genomen. Het gebouw werd in 1992 gesloten en gesloopt. | in de trant van de Amsterdamse School
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The former Elthetokerk was a Reformed church building at the corner of Insulindeweg and Kramatweg in the Indische Buurt in Amsterdam-Oost.

overrides.name: Artis
overrides.text: Founded in 1838 by three zoology enthusiasts, it is the oldest zoo in the Netherlands. The last quagga in captivity died here in 1883; nobody realised it was the last one until years later.
overrides.sourceQuote: It is the oldest zoo in the Netherlands | The zoo was founded in 1838 by three zoology enthusiasts | The last quagga in captivity died at Artis on 12 August 1883, because all zebras were referred to as quagga, nobody realized this was the last quagga alive until years later.
overrides.replaces: Natura Artis Magistra (Latin for "Nature is the teacher of art"), commonly known just as Artis (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɑrtɪs]), is a zoo and botanical garden in the centre of Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Academie van Bouwkunst
overrides.text: Set up in 1908, it ended 40 years in which Amsterdam had no architecture school. Its teachers are practising designers, and students must work in the field while they study.
overrides.sourceQuote: In 1908 the Academy of Architecture Amsterdam was set up | At that time Amsterdam had been lacking an architecture school for 40 years already | The teachers at the Academy are practising designers | the requirement that students work in the field during their studies
overrides.replaces: The Academy of Architecture of Amsterdam (Dutch: Academie van Bouwkunst Amsterdam) is a Dutch postgraduate school in architecture located in Amsterdam. This school is the architecture division of the Amsterdam University of the Arts, the city's vocational university of arts.

overrides.name: Zuiderkerk Tower
overrides.text: Completed in 1614, the 68-metre tower belongs to the Zuiderkerk, designed by Hendrick de Keyser. Its largest bell, cast in 1511, is the oldest bell in Amsterdam.
overrides.sourceQuote: De Zuidertoren kwam pas in 1614 gereed en is 68 meter hoog. | Het ontwerp in renaissancestijl is van de Amsterdamse architect Hendrick Cornelisz de Keyser | werd al in 1511 gegoten door Willem en Jasper Moer | Deze oudste luidklok van Amsterdam
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Zuidertoren is the tower of the Zuiderkerk in Amsterdam.

overrides.name: De Hallen
overrides.text: Built in 1902-1905 as a tram depot, it served the city transport company until 1996 and is now a cultural centre. One of its cinemas has the interior of the old Cinema Parisien.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het centrum is gevestigd in de voormalige Remise Tollensstraat van de Gemeentetram Amsterdam, gebouwd in 1902-'05 en is tot 1996 in gebruik geweest bij het Gemeentevervoerbedrijf Amsterdam | In de Filmhallen is een zaal is ingericht met het interieur van de vroegere Cinema Parisien
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Hallen is a cultural center in the Kinkerbuurt in Amsterdam-West, with more than two million visitors per year.

overrides.name: Rialto
overrides.text: Jan van Schaik designed the building in 1920 for film enthusiast Anton Pieter du Mée. It hosts the biennial CinemAsia film festival.
overrides.sourceQuote: The building that Rialto occupies was built in 1920 and was designed by the architect Jan van Schaik commissioned by film enthusiast Anton Pieter du Mée. | The biennial CinemAsia film festival is also held there.
overrides.replaces: Rialto is a cinema at Ceintuurbaan in the De Pijp neighborhood in Amsterdam.

overrides.name: Groote Museum
overrides.text: It fills the first floor of Artis's main building of 1850-1855, home of the Zoological Museum until 1947. Queen Máxima reopened it in 2022 after a ten-year restoration.
overrides.sourceQuote: Het is gevestigd op de eerste verdieping van het voormalig hoofdgebouw van Artis | dat tussen 1850 en 1855 werd gebouwd. Oorspronkelijk fungeerde deze ruimte als het Zoölogisch Museum Amsterdam | In 1947 werd het museum gesloten | tussen 2012 en 2022 een grondige restauratie | Op 10 mei 2022 werd het museum officieel heropend door Koningin Máxima.
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Groote Museum is a museum on the Plantage Middenlaan in Amsterdam exploring the connections between people, animals, plants, microbes and the earth.

overrides.name: Het Nieuwe Verbond
overrides.text: M.J. Granpré Molière designed this church, consecrated in 1957, with a tower that was never built because the parish could not afford it.
overrides.sourceQuote: Hij werd in 1954/1955 ontworpen door de architect M.J. Granpré Molière. | Op 19 december 1957 wijdde Mgr. J.P. Huibers de kerk in. | Granpré Molière had aanvankelijk ook een kerktoren ingetekend; echter, de financiële situatie van de parochie was onvoldoende om nog extra circa 100.000 gulden vrij te maken. | maar de toren zou er nooit komen
overrides.translator: claude-opus-5-5 (hand-written from the quoted sentences; Dutch translated faithfully)
overrides.replaces: The Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-van-Lourdes church, today the Church of Het Nieuwe Verbond, is a Roman Catholic church in the garden city Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.
